paper_metadata.title: Laser Additive Manufactured V-Shaped and L-Shaped Ti65 Titanium Alloy Interfaces and High-Temperature Performance
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: This study examines the microstructural characteristics, mechanical properties, and high-temperature performance of Ti65 titanium alloy fabricated via laser additive manufacturing (LAM).

evidence.quote: The specific parameters for the L-shaped joining process were as follows: laser power of 2000 W, scanning speed of 10 mm/s, layer height of 0.5 mm, hatch spacing of 2 mm, powder feed rate of 0.8 r/min, and a short-edge scanning strategy was employed for continuous deposition.
Following the laser additive joining process, all samples underwent post-process heat treatment at 700°C for 4 hours, followed by air coolin (AC).

This study examines the microstructural characteristics, mechanical properties, and high-temperature performance of Ti65 titanium alloy fabricated via laser additive manufacturing (LAM).

The specific parameters for the L-shaped joining process were as follows: laser power of 2000 W, scanning speed of 10 mm/s, layer height of 0.5 mm, hatch spacing of 2 mm, powder feed rate of 0.8 r/min, and a short-edge scanning strategy was employed for continuous deposition.
Following the laser additive joining process, all samples underwent post-process heat treatment at 700°C for 4 hours, followed by air coolin (AC).
Samples 2 and 3 were prepared to assess the interface bonding strength of the V-shaped joint at room temperature and 650°C, respectively.

The V-shaped laser joining process employed the following parameters: an initial layer laser power of 2000 W, a fill layer power of 2400 W, scanning speed of 10 mm/s, layer height of 0.5 mm, hatch spacing of 2 mm, and a powder feed rat 0.8 r/min.
After laser additive joining, all V-shaped specimens were subjected to post-processing heat treatment at 700°C for 4 hours, followed by air cooling.

After laser additive joining, all V-shaped specimens were subjected to post-processing heat treatment at 700°C for 4 hours, followed by air cooling.
